raw_response:
*My wife and me, we're both getting on in years. Kids moved to the city long ago. Fifteen mu is what we've got, same as always. Let me think through what I'm doing this year, same way I've done it most years.*

---

**My land split**

I keep about 9 mu for the wheat-maize back-to-back, and the other 6 mu I put in cotton. Cotton's harder on the body — all that picking through autumn — but we've done it so long it's hard to stop. My nephew comes a few days in October to help us pick when it's at its busiest. Wheat and maize are easier — hire the neighbor with the combine, hire his planter too. I can't swing the scythe or push a hand seeder anymore.

**Wheat (the 9 mu)**

Put it in around the 10th of October, like always. First cold rain of autumn, that's the sign. Before planting I broadcast two bags of that 15-15-15 compound per mu — two bags per mu, that's what my father did and that's what I do. Come spring when the wheat greens up and starts jointing, I'll top it off with about 20 jin of urea per mu. Water it three times through the year if the sky stays dry — once in early spring when it wakes up, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. The well still works fine but the electric is more expensive every year. Last year I got about 400 kg per mu. I figure about the same this year if nothing goes wrong. The flour is for us, the straw my neighbor takes for his sheep, and whatever grain is left I sell.

**Maize (same 9 mu, after wheat)**

Combine comes, wheat is out, one week later the maize has to be in the ground. No time to breathe. Hire the no-till planter — that's the way everyone does it now. I buy hybrid seed from the agricultural supply shop in town, about 50 yuan a mu. One and a half bags of compound at planting, then when it's knee-high I spread about 30 jin of urea per mu. One watering usually does it if the summer rains come on time. Sometimes I spray for corn borer if I see them. Maize gives 450 kg per mu in a regular year.

**Cotton (the 6 mu)**

Planted late April when the soil warms up. I saved seed from last year — why buy when last year's cotton did alright. Plowed the land in March. Put down compound fertilizer before planting, one and a half bags per mu, and when it's flowering I topdress more urea. The bollworm is the big worry — I spray two or three times through the summer, the village store sells what everyone uses. Water twice if it's a dry year. Then starting early September, my wife and me start picking. We pick what we can, pick again two weeks later, and once more in late October. Nephew comes for 5 days in the heaviest stretch. About 250 kg of lint per mu if the weather holds. Cotton prices haven't been great these last few years but I'm not about to change what I know.

**What I don't do**

I don't buy the fancy controlled-release fertilizer the rich farmers use. I don't test the soil — no one around here does, soil's been this soil for a thousand years. I don't chase every new thing the extension fellow brings around. If old Wang next door tries something and it works, I might try it next year. Otherwise, I do what I've always done.
